name: tldraw
tagline: An infinite-canvas whiteboard and drawing app, also sold as an embeddable SDK for developers.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. The public app is free to use; revenue comes from commercial SDK licensing, which is quoted rather than listed as a simple monthly seat price.

verdictSummary: A personal infinite canvas is a real one-sitting build: pan, zoom, freehand ink, a few shapes, text, selection, local save, PNG export. What you will not reproduce in one session is the part tldraw is actually famous for, which is the feel: arrow bindings that stay glued to shapes as you drag them, snapping and alignment guides, smooth pressure-sensitive ink, undo that never surprises you, and a canvas that stays at 60fps with a thousand shapes on it. Multiplayer cursors and conflict-free shared editing are a separate project entirely. There is also the awkward fact that tldraw's editor is source-available, so the honest move for a personal tool is often to run theirs rather than clone it. Build your own if you want a tiny sketchpad you fully control; do not build your own if you want the tldraw editing experience.
coreLoopDIY: An infinite pannable, zoomable canvas where you draw freehand, drop rectangles, ellipses, arrows and text, move and delete things, and have it all persist locally with PNG export.
requirements: No accounts, no server, no API keys
whatYouLose: Arrow bindings, snapping, and alignment guides that make diagramming feel effortless
Real-time multiplayer with cursors, presence and conflict resolution
Polished ink quality with pressure and velocity smoothing
Shape library, frames, embeds, sticky notes, and the long tail of tools
Robust undo/redo history across every operation, plus performance at thousands of shapes
moatNotes: The moat is interaction quality, thousands of tiny decisions about hit testing, bindings and pointer handling that only show up when you try to copy them.
whyPeopleStillPay: Almost nobody pays for tldraw as a whiteboard; they pay to embed its editor in their own product, and that is a completely different calculation. Writing a canvas engine that handles bindings, nested groups, text editing, touch, stylus, undo and multiplayer is a multi-quarter effort for a competent team, so a license is cheap by comparison. For personal sketching the free app or a self-hosted copy already covers it, which is why the DIY case here is more about learning than about saving money.
notes: You can clone the sketchpad in an evening and never get the arrows to feel right. The moat is interaction polish, not features.
prompt:
Build a local-first infinite canvas whiteboard as a single web app. No accounts, no server, no telemetry, no third-party APIs.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Vite + React + TypeScript
- Zustand for state
- perfect-freehand for ink smoothing
- idb-keyval for persistence in IndexedDB
- Plain CSS, no UI framework

Rendering:
- Render shapes as SVG inside a single viewport container, with a camera state of { x, y, zoom }.
- Space+drag or middle-mouse drag pans; ctrl/cmd+wheel and trackpad pinch zoom, clamped between 0.1x and 8x.
- Draw a faint dot grid that scales with zoom.

Tools in the toolbar: select, hand, draw, rectangle, ellipse, arrow, text, eraser.
- Draw: capture pointer events including pressure, run points through perfect-freehand, store the raw points so strokes can be re-rendered at any zoom.
- Shapes: click-drag to create, shift constrains to square/circle.
- Arrow: simple two-point arrow with a head. Do NOT attempt shape binding.
- Text: click to place, edit inline with a contenteditable, single font.
- Select: click to select, shift+click to add, drag-marquee for multi-select, drag to move, one bounding box with 8 resize handles, delete/backspace removes.

Required behaviors:
- Undo/redo with cmd+z and shift+cmd+z, implemented as an array of document snapshots capped at 100 entries.
- Autosave the document to IndexedDB, debounced 300ms, and reload it on startup.
- Export the whole canvas to PNG via canvas rasterization of the SVG, and export/import the document as a .json file.
- Keyboard shortcuts: v, h, d, r, o, a, t, e for tools.

Explicitly out of scope: multiplayer, cloud sync, auth, comments, shape libraries, embeds, frames, groups, mobile-specific UI.

Deliverables: working app on npm run dev, a README with shortcuts, and .env.example only if any secret is ever needed (it should not be).
